crit: 12 imbalanced UCI datasets (multiclass ones binarized one-versus-rest) plus randomly undersampled versions to generate datasets with even higher imbalance ratios (factors 2-20, only if at least eight minority samples remain); 19 imbalanced KEEL datasets 'selected' with no stated reason; ten scikit-learn variations of the artificial MADELON dataset, which poses a difficult binary classification problem; five 2-D toy datasets introduced to demonstrate the properties of k-means SMOTE.
notes: binarised_by 'both': UCI multiclass sets binarized by the authors (smallest class vs rest); KEEL sets are ready-made two-class splits (e.g. yeast-2_vs_8, full names such as yeast-0-5-6-7-9_vs_4 and cleveland-0_vs_4 appear in Fig. 8). minority_rule records the explicit UCI rule; KEEL splits are repository-defined; for the two make_circles/make_moons toy sets the minority is induced by the authors (750 per class, one class undersampled to 200), which could also be read as an Induced profile. Count issues: text says 19 KEEL datasets but Table 2 has 20 KEEL rows; yeast2 and yeast-2_vs_4 have identical rows (8, 514, 51, 463, 9.08); Fig. 8 shows poker-9_vs_7 (absent from Table 2) and no yeast2. Undersampled versions (e.g. heart6, pima4, ecoli6, breast_tissue2, glass4, pima2) are omitted from Table 2 and only named in Figs. 8-9 (images, no characteristics). The 90-dataset total is stated in the abstract and on p.18. No per-dataset numeric results table: per-dataset AUPRC only in Fig. 8 (image). Toy datasets A, B, C were created for this work and released (v0.0.2 toy_datasets.tar.gz). pdf p.1 is a cover page, so printed p.N = pdf p.N+1.
